correctness.rationale: For any finite connected graph Markov positivity couples adjacent heat laws and yields the diameter upper bound. Strict nonattainment for any fixed diameter-at-least-two finite graph follows from strictly positive kernel overlap for every positive time, the value one at time zero, continuity, and decay to constants. Even/odd rooted tree constructions have diameter exactly D and explicit edge-one-Lipschitz witness functions. Independent Poisson clocks at rates b and one prove the lower bounds and their fixed-diameter b-to-infinity limits; no computation substitutes for an infinite proof. The standalone numerical script checked 64 quotiented cases and 12 exact full-graph versus quotient comparisons.

value.rationale: This is not merely the elementary Markov diameter estimate: it establishes its exact optimality among all finite graphs of every prescribed diameter via highly branched finite trees at vanishing times, proves strict nonattainment on any single finite graph, and gives quantitative uniform-in-time witnesses. It answers a natural stability question with diameter as the only known geometric datum for an important positive semigroup; the construction shows how arbitrarily strong transient local-gradient amplification can coexist with positivity and eventual mixing. No claim is made about exact individual graph time profiles.
